title: Residency, KMS, and Synthetic Data Constraints - Praxis Lending Discovery
summary: Initial compliance and residency discovery focused on: where inference data can live, KMS/HSM key residency, log retention/redaction, and use of synthetic data for model evaluation. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; strong preference for proof of no PII exfiltration and retention guarantees.
topics: Synthetic data usage for PII-free benchmarks
Pilot scopes and next steps for benchmarks
action_items: Ethan Cole - prepare pilot runbook (latency/cost knobs + dataset sanitization steps) - due 2028-05-16
Maya Ortiz - send SOC2 type II report, security pitch deck, and private deployment checklist - due 2028-05-11
Asha Patel (Praxis) - provide sample data profile and regulatory constraints doc (PII fields + retention windows) - due 2028-05-13
next_steps: Schedule 2-hour pilot planning session (benchmarks + success criteria)
Redwood to propose Dedicated pilot pricing and duration
Customer to share sanitized sample records and compliance boundary doc
transcript:
Header: 2028-05-09 15:30 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Ortiz, Ethan Cole (Redwood); Lila Hammond, Marcus Zhou, Asha Patel, Devon Reyes (Praxis)

[00:00] Maya Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for carving time, this is Maya from Redwood Inference, our AE. Ethan is my SE and will walk through the technical fit. Quick goals for today: understand your residency constraints, KMS needs, and whether synthetic data is sufficient for our pilot.

[00:27] Marcus Zhou: Thanks Maya. We're mainly worried about two things: first, where is the data processed and logged, and second, can we demo without exposing PII. We're a lending platform so PCI-ish plus PII and some regional regulators.

[00:45] Lila Hammond: Hi all. From security side: SOC2, SSO, key management, and log redaction are our top blockers. We need a clear statement of which logs leave our VPC and what we can redact.

[01:05] Ethan Cole: Great. At a high level Redwood has three hosting modes: Hosted (multi-tenant API), Dedicated (reserved gpu pools with isolation), and Private (VPC/private control plane). For residency and key escrow we usually recommend Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads because keys can be customer-controlled and logs can stay in region.

[01:38] Devon Reyes: Can you explain what 'keys customer-controlled' actually means? HSM or bring-your-own-key?

[01:46] Ethan Cole: Yes, two options. For Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS using your cloud provider KMS, we can integrate with your HSM for on-prem. For Private we can do full HSM-backed keys in your VPC and we can configure key rotation policies. Note—some of this is manual provisioning during the private install.

[02:12] Asha Patel: A big question: during inference are prompts or traces ever stored in plaintext on Redwood systems? We have regulators asking about full end-to-end custody.

[02:25] Maya Ortiz: Short answer: by default hosted mode retains limited logs for billing and debugging; we offer log redaction and a no-logs option for Dedicated/Private depending on contract. For Private you can configure log sinks to your own S3 in-region and disable retention on Redwood side. We'll send the log retention matrix.

[02:49] Lila Hammond: What about model caching / KV cache? Does any sensitive context ever land on shared disks? We need deterministic answers for audit.

[03:00] Ethan Cole: Good callout. The runtime uses a KV cache for decoding performance. In Dedicated we can scope cache to the customer's GPU pool only; in Private it's fully inside your network. For Hosted we do prefix caching with strict TTLs and we can enable prefix kv encryption. I will add specifics to the runbook — sorry if the phrase 'kay vee cache' sounded odd in auto notes.

[03:30] Marcus Zhou: We also plan to run model evaluation with synthetic data that mimics worst-case PII patterns. Can Redwood accept synthetic datasets for benchmarks or do you need real anonymized samples?

[03:44] Ethan Cole: Synthetic is fine and often preferred for privacy. Two caveats: 1) synthetic must exercise the same token length distributions and entity patterns for performance parity; 2) if you need exact parity for model quality regression, we recommend a small, controlled redacted set under a legal agreement. For the pilot we can start with synthetic.

[04:08] Lila Hammond: On the legal side, will Redwood sign our DPA and can you support data residency clauses limiting data to eu-west-1 and us-east-1 only?

[04:20] Maya Ortiz: We have a standard DPA and can negotiate residency addenda. For Dedicated we can pin to regions and for Private you're fully in control. There is some nuance with fallbacks: for example if a Dedicated zone is degraded we can route to another region only if you permit it in the routing policy — otherwise requests may queue or fallback to a colder instance.

[04:48] Devon Reyes: What's the visibility into audit logs? We need immutable audit trails and SAML event logs forwarded to our SIEM.

[04:58] Ethan Cole: We can stream audit logs to your syslog/S3/Splunk instance in near real-time; retention policy is pluggable. For Private we can keep all audit logs in your account. For Dedicated, logs can be exported to customer buckets and we can enable log compression and encryption with your keys.

[05:20] Marcus Zhou: Any compliance artifacts you'd share? SOC2 Type II, penetration test reports, ISO statements?

[05:29] Maya Ortiz: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and the most recent penetration test summary. For Private deployments we also provide a deployment checklist with hardening steps. I'll attach those to the follow-up email.

[05:47] Asha Patel: Retention windows: regulators require 7 years for certain records. We're not going to keep full transcripts that long, but need an auditable ledger of decisions. Can Redwood implement log tiering and retention labels?

[06:05] Ethan Cole: Yep — tiered retention is supported. You can set short-lived raw transcript retention and export structured metadata (timestamps, audit events, redaction hashes) to an immutable store for long-term retention. We also support redact-on-write policies where PII fields are removed before storage.

[06:36] Lila Hammond: Key escrow — we have an internal policy requiring escrow for some regulators. Do you support escrow with a neutral third party or an enterprise key escrow flow?

[06:48] Maya Ortiz: We support third-party escrow arrangements for Private installs; for Dedicated we can agree on an escrow procedure and we can also provide split-key escrow models. We'll need legal to sync on specifics.

[07:05] Marcus Zhou: For the pilot we're leaning to Dedicated reserved capacity in us-east-1 with keys in our KMS and logs exported to our S3. We want to validate latency under our worst-case 2k token sequences and also run the synthetic PII dataset.

[07:22] Ethan Cole: That's a good scoped pilot. For success criteria let's be explicit: 1) 95th percentile latency under X ms for 2k tokens; 2) no PII persisted in Redwood-managed logs; 3) reproducible audit trail to your SIEM. We'll capture these in the runbook.

[07:42] Lila Hammond: Also need to validate redaction works end-to-end — can you run an internal test where you intentionally send obviously redactable PII and show the artifact is removed?

[07:52] Ethan Cole: Yes, we can include a redaction proof step. We'll record before/after artifacts and route the before artifacts only to your private S3 if you want the forensic trail.

[08:08] Maya Ortiz: Quick timeline conversation — you indicated procurement windows in Q3, is that still accurate?

[08:16] Marcus Zhou: Q3 procurement is target but we want a pilot in the next 3 weeks to build the internal case. Ideally run the pilot for 2 weeks then present to procurement.

[08:30] Maya Ortiz: Great — immediate next steps: I will send SOC2 + pentest summary + private deployment checklist and a proposed Dedicated pilot scope. Ethan will draft the pilot runbook and include the synthetic dataset requirements and success metrics. Asha will share the sample data profile.

[08:52] Asha Patel: Sounds good. One last quick question — do you encrypt model weights at rest, and can you certify that third-party model variants don't pull telemetry from inputs?

[09:04] Ethan Cole: Model weights at rest are encrypted with customer-controlled KMS when on Dedicated/Private. For hosted models we enforce encryption at rest and strict telemetry policies; we can provide a telemetry statement. We also have Redwood-verified model variants with limited telemetry.

[09:24] Lila Hammond: Ok thanks everyone. We'll review the artifacts and aim to have the sample data and decision criteria to you by next week.

[09:34] Maya Ortiz: Thank you all — we'll follow up with deliverables and schedule the pilot planning session.

[09:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription mislabels a couple of technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" -> "kay vee cache"), occasional speaker overlap.
